page: Microsoft Azure E16-8s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, the server features 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, resulting in 2 threads per core. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 35 MB L3 caches. This instance includes a bundled 262 GB local SSD and is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between compute power and memory capacity. The server exhibits poor single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, falling into the bottom 10%, and weak multi-core CPU performance in the bottom 25%. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scores fall into the bottom 25%. However, memory bandwidth remains stable, with both small-block cached reads and large-block uncached reads and writes scoring in the middle 50%. Passmark memory and database operations also achieve average ratings, alongside Redis SET operations which reach 6.25 million operations per second.

Given the high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core, the E16-8s_v3 is structured for memory-intensive workloads rather than compute-heavy operations. The qualitative cost efficiency of this hardware profile lies in its high memory allocation relative to the active vCPU count, allowing users to host large datasets in memory without paying for unneeded compute cores. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers, and memory-optimized enterprise applications that require high memory density but can tolerate moderate CPU performance.
